tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with concrete trigger phrases users might say (e.g., 'why is my CloudTrail bill so high', 'reduce CloudTrail costs'), and covers explicit trigger contexts including indirect phrasing like unexpected cost increases. It also briefly summarizes scope/implementation at the end but stays concise overall.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize CloudTrail spend, or reports an unexpected CloudTrail cost or usage increase. Activate on requests like "why is my CloudTrail bill so high", "reduce CloudTrail costs"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what CloudTrail is) and focuses on billing specifics, workflow, and non-obvious rules like the dedup-vs-filtering interaction. Sections are dense but each sentence carries domain-specific information the agent needs.
tests.evidence: Management events: the first copy per Region is free; every additional copy is billed. Duplicate management-event trails are the most common overspend.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (API call tables, opportunity check definitions, billing tables) are all pushed into references/ files, loaded conditionally. The body only keeps a short billing summary bullet list, not a full table.
tests.evidence: For the full charge-by-charge table and the detailed billing consequences the checks rely on, load references/billing-model.md when you need to decide whether a specific trail copy is free or paid, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files (api-inventory.md, billing-model.md, opportunities.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear trigger condition for when to load the file.
tests.evidence: load [references/api-inventory.md](references/api-inventory.md) when...For the exact API calls to make, what each returns, and the per-trail fields to record

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative paths from the skill root with the references/ prefix, no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-sensitive operations (safety boundaries, dedup-vs-filtering rule) are prescriptive with exact do/don't rules, while flexible tasks like scope selection and volume signal gathering explain rationale and allow agent judgment.
tests.evidence: Never recommend reducing the single authoritative security trail below the organization's logging requirements. When in doubt, recommend converting a duplicate to data-events-only rather than deleting it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple signals/tools are presented for usage collection, Cost Explorer is clearly designated as the preferred/default signal with others as fallbacks.
tests.evidence: This is the most direct dollar signal — prefer it when the role has Cost Explorer access.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (identify scope, inventory, collect signals, analyze, validate, report) applicable to any CloudTrail cost review, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated 'Known Quirks' section documents concrete, non-obvious pitfalls specific to CloudTrail billing and shadow trails.
tests.evidence: Organizations trails appear as shadow trails in member accounts — set includeShadowTrails=true and do not double-count them as member-created duplicates.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and provides an assets/report-template.md referenced for that purpose.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large template exists inline in the body; only a small severity definitions table (5 rows) is present, well under 20 lines, and the full report template is externalized to assets/.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is linked in the body.
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report. [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md)

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies clearly when to load it — when generating the final report.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from skill root with assets/ prefix.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is procedural with dependent steps and correctly uses the checkbox '- [ ] Step N:' format as required.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1: Identify target scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2: Inventory trails and event data stores.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check findings for double-counting and traceability before producing the report, satisfying the validation loop requirement.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm no finding double-counts savings already captured by a §4.1 dedup, verify each management-event filtering finding applies only to a paid copy that is being kept...
